gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX S5000 has two different solar inputs (Input 1: 11–60 V, 17 A, 1,000 W; Input 2: 16–165 V, 17 A, 2,000 W), so the S5000 + 2× 400 W kit is the only kit we link under $4,000 whose station can take a panel string above 60 V today, while the BLUETTI Apex 300 kits are held to 12–60 V and 20 A per input.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited), the Anker SOLIX kit collection (cited), Lights On Labs, PowerSized, Prepared States and Dealectric's own under-$3,000 page; solargenadvisor.com would not open (certificate error). Rivals already hold this kind of fact for other kits: Prepared States gives the Apex 300 window (1,200 W, 12–60 V, 20 A per input; two SORA 500 make 98.2 V in series and 26.6 A in parallel, so one panel per input), StormWatts gives the Apex 200 ports (XT60 1,000 W 12–60 V 25 A, MC4 2,000 W 60–280 V), and Dealectric's under-$3,000 page gives the Elite 2× 350 W parallel-only limit. None gives the S5000's input windows, and Anker's own kit collection page has no solar input figures at all. The finding is incomplete: I could not open a maker page with the Voc and Isc of the 400 W panel in the S5000 bundle, so the string arithmetic for that kit is not done.
decides: It confirms the S5000 + 2× 400 W ($3,599.99) as the kit in the $3,000–$4,000 band with solar headroom: 800 W of panels against 3,000 W of input, and a 16–165 V input that takes panels in series. The Apex 300 kits need one large panel per 12–60 V input. On the Apex 200 + B500K + 2× 500 W ($3,986.20 link price, pre-order), the two panels must go in series on the MC4 input: by the rivals' figures 98.2 V sits inside 60–280 V, 26.6 A in parallel exceeds the 25 A XT60 input, and one panel alone (49.1 V) is under the MC4 input's 60 V floor. One thing to recheck before the S5000 kit is named the ships-now pick: Anker's S5000 product page, as read today, says orders placed on or after November 6 ship in 11–12 weeks and that orders including the 400 W panel ship separately, which conflicts with the "ships now" in the kit table. The page text gave no year for those dates. Anker also lists 32–104°F as the S5000's charging temperature, so a unit in an unheated garage will not take solar below freezing.
